threshold_mw.value: 20 MW: a facility primarily engaged in NAICS 518210 (data centers) that uses or is able to use 20 MW or more (Schedule 401 as filed: load registering 20,000 kW or greater, or Reserved Capacity of 20,000 kW or greater). Sites with common ownership within 2,500 feet of each other or served by the same substation count as one, and commonly owned data centers anywhere in the territory have their Contract Demand summed

cites.quote: a facility that uses or is able to use 20 megawatts or more and is primarily engaged in providing a service described under the 2022 North American Industry Classification System Code 518210
whose electric service load registers 20,000 kW or greater or whose Reserved Capacity is 20,000 kW or greater

If two or more sites have common ownership and are within 2,500 feet of each other or are served by the same substation, the sites will be treated as one for the purpose of capacity allocation and the qualification for a LEUF Agreement

min_demand.value: No minimum percentage is printed. Standard LEUF Agreements carry (1) a Reservation Charge based on Contract Demand, paid monthly over the term and set to recover the full cost of the generation, storage and network facilities needed to serve the load, or, where the customer chooses its own resources, direct reimbursement plus a Portfolio Risk Management Charge based on Contract Demand and a System Firming and Balancing Charge at 33 percent of Schedule 48 System Fixed Generation; (2) a Peak Demand Charge at the OATT Schedule 1, Schedule 3 and NITS rates on the month's highest demand; (3) the Schedule 300 Excess Demand Charge

cites.section: IV.E.5 Compensation for generation and storage resources
cites.quote: a Reservation Charge based on the Contract Demand and paid monthly during the term
a Portfolio Risk Management Charge that will be based on Contract Demand
a System Firming and Balancing Charge set at 33 percent of System Fixed Generation applicable to Schedule 48
a Peak Demand Charge that is based on the customer's highest demand during the month
the New LEUF is subject to the Schedule 300 Excess Demand Charge

contract_term.value: Minimum 10 years, maximum 30 years, inclusive of any ramp period; renewals at least 10 years

cites.quote: Paragraph 24 of the stipulation sets a minimum 10-year LEUF Agreement term, with a maximum term of 30 years, inclusive of any ramp period. Paragraph 31 provides that LEUF Agreement renewals will be at least 10 years in length.

collateral.value: At the company's election, sufficient creditworthiness or posted collateral to cover the customer's Exit Fee; creditworthiness means senior unsecured long-term debt rated A- or higher (S&P or Fitch), A (low) or higher (DBRS) or A3 or higher (Moody's), or an equivalent internal rating; the amount is reassessed every two years. Network Upgrades needed for the load are paid up front by the LEUF, except Qualified Network Upgrades (230 kV and above, on the WECC critical path list, with less than 80 percent of known capacity needs from LEUFs), which are paid as a monthly fee on the LEUF's share

cites.quote: Paragraph 29 of the stipulation provides that a LEUF shall, at the company's election, be required to provide sufficient creditworthiness or post collateral to cover the customer's Exit Fee.
The senior unsecured long term debt of a customer has a rating of A- or higher by Standard & Poor's or Fitch, A (low) or higher by DBRS, or A3 or higher by Moody's Investor Services, Inc.
The stipulation states that the amount will be reassessed every two years to reflect the customer's current Exit Fee.

cites.section: IV.E.1 Line extension and network upgrade costs
cites.quote: any Network Upgrades (as defined in Rule 13, including bulk transmission) required to serve the New LEUF's load will be paid for upfront by the New LEUF

exit_fee.value: Exit Fee set to recover company-funded infrastructure: net book value of company-funded infrastructure, net cost of customer-specific power or tolling agreements, the Reservation Charge for the remainder of the contract, and the net cost of removing facilities no longer needed; refunded pro rata if another large customer takes the capacity within three years (the removal cost is not refunded)

cites.quote: The Exit Fee will include the net book value of company-funded infrastructure, the net cost of customer-specific power/tolling agreements, the Reservation Charge for the remainder of the customer's contract, and the net cost of removing facilities no longer needed.
If another large customer takes service within three years of an exiting LEUF's departure, the Exit Fee will be refunded by a pro-rata share of the capacity assumed by the new large customer.

study_timeline.value: No study deadline is set (the stipulating parties said a standard deadline is not possible). Company practice as testified: initial load interconnection system impact study in no more than six months after the required documents and study payment. LEUF Agreement filed within 45 days of execution; if none is executed within 180 days of completion of the service study, either party may file an unexecuted agreement; Commission review 90 days (standard agreement) or 180 days (non-conforming), extendable for good cause. Engineering studies are funded separately by the LEUF

cites.quote: the length of time needed to complete a study is variable based on the specific attributes of the LEUF request, so it is not possible to establish a standard deadline for when the study must be completed
The company strives to complete an initial load interconnection system impact study in no more than six months after the customer has submitted required documents and the study payment.

within 45 days after execution, a LEUF Agreement will be filed with the Commission for approval. If the parties have not executed a LEUF Agreement within 180 days of completion of the service study, either party may file an unexecuted LEUF Agreement and request Commission resolution of disputed terms.
the Commission will have 90 days to approve or reject a standard LEUF Agreement, or 180 days to approve or reject a non-conforming LEUF Agreement
Engineering studies are funded separately and are allocated fully to the New LEUF.

connection_timeline.value: No duration printed. The LEUF Agreement must specify the date or estimated date service begins (Schedule 401 as filed); LEUFs are interconnected in the order in which they execute LEUF Agreements, subject to agreed construction timelines and system constraints

cites.section: Proposed Original Sheet No. 401-2, Special Condition 3.f
cites.quote: The Large Energy Use Facility Agreement shall specify the date or estimated date that the Company will begin to provide service to the Customer.
LEUF customers will be interconnected in the order in which they execute a LEUF Agreement, subject to agreed-upon construction timelines, and system constraints

rows.notes: Advice No. 25-015 (filed 2 October 2025, asking 1 January 2026) is permanently suspended (Order 26-443, p. 41, ordering paragraph 1); new tariffs consistent with the stipulation are due by 24 November 2026, effective 1 January 2027; the compliance sheets were not filed or read on 13 November 2026, and rehearing may be sought within 60 days. Order No. 25-516 (16 December 2025) suspended the filing for investigation. Other stipulation terms: a 1 cent per kWh community energy benefits charge on LEUFs over 100 MW (the order's page 12 prints '1 cent/kW'); a $25,000 nonrefundable application fee; new incremental resources must be non-emitting; already energized New LEUFs may not exceed their highest measured peak until a LEUF Agreement is approved; PacifiCorp must file a tariff for LEUFs not on Schedule 401 within 60 days of the rate effective date of UE 470; a biennial LEUF report, the first due 31 March 2027; the LEUF queue is reported to the Commission confidentially (no public count yet). DCC opposed the stipulation; ADS and NewSun commented. The Oregon PUC's POWER Act report (2026) says Pacific Power's earlier large load tariff came in UE 433 (row: Rule 13). Leads not used: an Idaho Capital Sun article on the settlement (refused by robots). PacifiCorp's testimony also gives its engineering study thresholds by state (PAC/200, Eller/4 to 6, pp. 66 to 68): 20 MW in Pacific Power states, 25 MW in Rocky Mountain Power states.
